I have repeatedly been given incorrect prescriptions, been scoffed at for understanding my own chronic illness, and even told outright medically inaccurate statements (including that women “can’t ride bikes”).

As someone living with a chronic condition, I expect at minimum to be listened to and taken seriously. Instead, I’ve been dismissed, patronised, and made to feel as though advocating for my own health is an inconvenience. There was one great doctor here that made this surgery worthwhile who, unfortunately for me, is on maternity leave now.

The situation is made significantly worse by the receptionist, who behaves as though she is the gatekeeper to medical care rather than an administrative support. She routinely refuses to book GP appointments, overrides requests that have been explicitly agreed between my doctor and me for managing flare-ups, and refuses to listen or engage respectfully. This is not only inappropriate but actively obstructs patient care.

This practice demonstrates a worrying lack of respect for patients, poor understanding of chronic illness, and a culture where patients are dismissed rather than supported. I would strongly advise anyone — particularly those with long-term or complex health conditions — to think very carefully before registering
